findings.summary: TVA.I8's docstring says it is `tl.int32` values (the type of tl.program_id and tl.arange); I8 is IntV true 8, and the text belongs to TVA.I32, which has none
findings.detail: lean/TVA/Lang/Scalar.lean:103-106 puts the docstring '`tl.int32` values, the type of `tl.program_id`, `tl.arange` and most index arithmetic.' on `abbrev I8 := IntV true 8`; `I32 := IntV true 32` (line 106) has no docstring. The claim reader hashes library docstrings as part of what the library means, and claim.md of this kernel shows the text under `TVA.I8` in the cones of `model` and `spec`, so a reader of any claim sees `I8` described as the 32-bit index type. A prover who took the docstring at its word would model an index as 8 bits. This kernel is not affected: its model uses `I32` (work/Names4.lean prints `TVA.I32 = TVA.IntV Bool.true 32`). Resolution: move the docstring to `I32`, and give `I8` its own (`tl.int8`).
findings.evidence: claim.md, section 4, 'Library definitions this item reaches': `TVA.I8` (TVA.Lang.Scalar): `tl.int32` values, the type of `tl.program_id`, `tl.arange` and most index arithmetic.

findings.summary: Scope 11's reuse clause names the source, compile-time values and settings, not the runtime arguments' specialisation; its example 'a repeated launch of the same instance' reads narrower
findings.detail: Scope 11 (the page, and the docstring of Rules.Compiler.Faithful) admits code 'compiled for it, ... or earlier for the same source, compile-time values and settings (a repeated launch of the same instance)'. Two readings go wrong. (1) Too wide: the compile-time values it lists are the constexprs and an integer 1 or None, so the clause read literally admits code compiled for another specialisation of a runtime argument (an integer a multiple of 16 or not, a pointer 16-byte aligned or not: SEMANTICS.md, 'Scalar arguments'; point 6's classes), which point 6's evidence shows can write past n (n = 1001 run on code compiled for n = 1024). A JIT launch is specialised on its own arguments (SEMANTICS.md, 'Scalar arguments': a multiple of 16 is marked so for the compiler), so for this kernel's launches I read this as wording, but the rule's text should not admit it. (2) Too narrow: the example can be read as the only reuse allowed. Then every launch of a new size after the first, such as this kernel's benchmark launches at 2^13 ... 2^27 elements, which run the code compiled for the first launch (same BLOCK_SIZE = 1024, n a multiple of 16), would be outside the rule, though n is not a compile-time value. Resolution: say 'or earlier for the same source, compile-time values, classes of the runtime arguments (point 6's) and settings: a repeated launch, or a launch of another instance in the same classes, such as another size'. The kernel's README repeats the example (Modelling decisions); I do not block on it.
